item.title: Lectern 1.9.0
item.description: Subjects, lecture notes, flashcards, quizzes and a planner in one Mac app.
item.content:encoded:
Lecture notes in Summary Studio, Process Lectures, smarter default models and automatic search by meaning

Changed

  • Generate Notes is now Summary Studio's "Lecture notes" type: overview, objectives, detailed notes by topic with slide citations and practice questions, key terms (into the subject glossary) and a summary, built from the same checked facts as every summary and checked against the slides. Notes from a link use it too.
  • Process Lectures… (Study menu, and a subject or folder's right-click menu) makes lecture notes, summaries, flashcards or Study Packs for every lecture in one place, replacing Summarise All…, Make Study Packs, Generate Flashcards for All Lectures and the Processing Queue menu item.
  • Auto is the default model for each task: your chosen model writes notes, summaries and chat; a small, fast model finds and checks facts and makes flashcards and quizzes (Haiku if you use Claude). Choices you made yourself are kept.
  • Search by meaning turns on by itself when an embedding model (such as embeddinggemma) is installed in Ollama; you can still turn it off.

Install: download Lectern.dmg, drag Lectern to Applications, then right-click it and choose Open the first time (the app isn't notarized).

item.title: Lectern 1.8.0
item.description: Subjects, lecture notes, flashcards, quizzes and a planner in one Mac app.
item.content:encoded:
Complete quality pass: faster, more reliable, easier to use, and a full Feature Guide

The "1.4.0" quality release (numbered 1.8.0 so it can update 1.7.0): a complete audit of every feature, with the fixes it led to. See AUDIT.md, FEATURES.md and BUGS.md in the source repository.

Added

  • Update Now in Settings → Updates: what's new, then download, check and install in one click, with progress and plain-English errors (Download Manually, Copy error details).
  • Help → Feature Guide: everything Lectern does, searchable, with Show Me buttons. Also as a PDF (Lectern User Guide).
  • Help → Troubleshoot…: rebuild the search index or embeddings, clear AI caches, check Ollama and models, reset the processing queue, reconnect the University folder, restore a backup, and Safe Mode (also by holding Option while Lectern opens).
  • Report a Problem… saves a diagnostics file to your Desktop (versions, settings, recent log, never your notes) for you to read before attaching it to the GitHub issue it opens.
  • Diagnostics (Settings, with advanced settings shown): index, queue, caches with Clear, AI use, Ollama status and the recent log; optional local-only counts of which features you use (off by default, never sent anywhere).
  • Settings search, a description of each section, Restore Defaults per section, and "Show advanced settings".
  • Keyboard Shortcuts is searchable and lists every shortcut.

Changed

  • Settings is a sidebar instead of ten tabs (Backup and Updates were hidden behind an overflow arrow).
  • Every AI action shows the same progress (with time left and Cancel) and the same error card with the way forward.
  • Background work pauses while the Mac sleeps, when Ollama stops, when the University folder goes missing or the disk is nearly full, and resumes afterwards; AI jobs with no progress for 10 minutes are stopped with Resume.
  • Summary Studio, the flashcard panel, the Planner, Search and subject pages adapt to small windows.
  • Reduce Motion and Increase Contrast are respected throughout, including in the editor.
  • Text alignment is ⌃⌘L/E/R/J and subscript ⇧⌘, (the old shortcuts were taken by menu commands and never worked).

Fixed

  • Text typed just before renaming or moving the open page was lost, and deleting the open page could bring it back.
  • Typing straight after creating a page could be thrown away.
  • An AI result put into the open page (a queued summary, a Study Pack, Insert in Summary Studio, flashcards, a planner tick) could overwrite what you'd typed in the last moment; switching pages straight after typing could also drop the last few words.
  • A page changed in another app or on another device while open in Lectern could be overwritten by the next autosave; both versions are now kept.
  • Changes made outside Lectern were ignored for University folders reached through a symlink, and pages there could get the wrong path.
  • Summaries of long lectures spend about a quarter of the time on Lectern's own processing (fact de-duplication was comparing every pair).
  • Transcripts get a timestamp about every 30 seconds instead of every 5 minutes.
  • Lecture pages re-read their slides every time they opened (and the suggestions bar did so on every redraw), slowing large lectures and growing memory.
  • Opening Settings → AI could freeze Lectern behind a Keychain password prompt; the Claude key is now read once.
  • Recent pages and the sidebar could keep entries for pages that no longer exist.
  • The Back and Forward tooltips showed the wrong shortcuts.
  • Release checks no longer touch the installed app's settings, Keychain or log, and the test suite no longer writes into your Lectern data.

Install: download Lectern.dmg, drag Lectern to Applications, then right-click it and choose Open the first time (the app isn't notarized).

item.title: Lectern 1.7.0
item.description: Subjects, lecture notes, flashcards, quizzes and a planner in one Mac app.
item.content:encoded:
More summary types (including same headings as the PDF), much better flashcard generation, Study Packs, auto-processing, phone review and more

This is the "1.3.0" feature release, numbered 1.7.0 so it can update 1.6.0.

Added

  • Quick summary types at the top of Summary Studio and in every file, page and folder's right-click menu (Summarise as…): Brief, Standard, Long/Detailed, Dot points, Same headings as the PDF, Slide by slide, Key points only, Exam revision (with practice questions after each section), Explain simply and Cheat sheet. "More types…" reaches every format. Pin and drag to reorder your favourites; your last type is remembered per subject.
  • Organise by: the source's own headings (PDF bookmarks, numbered headings like "2.3", heading styles or slide titles, each with its page or slide range, to the depth you choose, with tiny sections merged), by topic, in source order, slide by slide, by week or lecture, or by learning outcome. Review the detected headings first: skip, rename or merge them.
  • Any combination of type, format, length, organisation, level, focus and options works, with a plain-English description before you generate ("Brief dot points under each of the source's 12 headings, about 600 words").
  • Accurate lengths: summaries are checked against the target and condensed or expanded (from the cached facts) when more than 20% off. Word count and reading time are shown.
  • Content type (science/maths, programming, humanities, law/business, health/biology) is detected and changes how summaries and cards are written; you can change it.
  • Compare two summaries side by side with differences highlighted; every generated version stays in the page's summary history.
  • A new flashcard generator built from the checked facts on every slide: density from Light to Exhaustive (or a number), an estimate of cards and time, many card types (question/answer, definitions both ways, fill-in-the-blank, lists, processes, compare, scenarios, formulas, code, diagram labels as image occlusion, optional true/false) with a difficulty mix, quality rules (one idea, clear question, short answer, nothing given away), a faithfulness check against each card's source, and duplicate detection against your existing cards. A coverage report lists slides without cards with "Generate for These".
  • Every generated card keeps its page, slide number, a source excerpt (shown under "Source" on the back), an optional slide thumbnail, "Open Slide" and "Jump to Source", and automatic subject, week, topic and type tags.
  • Card review screen: grouped by slide with thumbnails, filters by type and topic, accept or reject per card or slide, inline editing, change a card's type, J/K/A/R/E and ⇧A, "Similar to an existing card" comparisons, or skip review for trusted batches.
  • Make cards from a page, a summary, a folder (via the Processing Queue), quiz mistakes, past-paper questions or active recall, and "Top Up" a page with cards only for slides that don't have any.
  • Study Packs: one click makes a summary, flashcards, a 10-question practice quiz and a one-page cheat sheet from the same cached facts, in the background (Quick, Standard and Exam prep presets, editable in Settings).
  • Auto-file new lectures: watch folders such as Downloads; slide files named with your unit codes are offered (or filed automatically) into the right subject and week, with optional Study Packs, custom name patterns, and an undo list in the Inbox.
  • Review on Phone: a QR code opens a mobile review page on your home Wi-Fi (tap to flip, Again/Hard/Good/Easy or swipe, add to Home Screen). Reviews sync straight back and are queued if the connection drops. A one-time key, local network only, off after 2 hours idle, with a menu bar indicator.
  • Anki: export any deck, page, folder or subject to .apkg (basic, reversed and cloze cards, tags, images and a Source field), and import .apkg packages and Anki text exports (review history optional).
  • Glossary hover: subject glossary terms in your notes show their definition on hover; ⌘-click opens where they were defined (can be turned off per page).
  • A suggestions bar on lecture pages (summarise, make cards, transcribe the recording, review due cards), recent actions in the command palette, Repeat Last Action (⇧⌘R), an AI Actions list with Undo for summaries and cards, and a quick AI settings button in the toolbar.

Changed

  • Start Reviews is now ⌥⇧⌘R (⇧⌘R repeats your last AI action).
  • Lengths: Standard is about 18%; new Brief (5%) and Long (45%).

Fixed

  • Making flashcards with a small local model could fail with "couldn't be read" on some lectures. The new generator writes cards from short, checked facts and never fails a whole lecture because of one bad reply.
  • Summaries could cite a fact to the wrong slide when a small model, re-reading missed slides, quoted something from a neighbouring slide. Those facts are now dropped instead of being relabelled.
  • (Found while benchmarking the new generator, before release.) Small local models sometimes copied the prompt's example cards. Those were rejected, but the facts then got no card at all. Each fact now falls back to a fill-in-the-blank card in its own words, and short, fact-packed readings get enough cards.
  • Title and section-divider slides no longer get a filler line in summaries just to "cover" them.

Benchmarks (llama3.2 3B on this Mac)

  • Flashcards, old generator → new at Standard (coverage of must-know facts / quality / duplicates / correct slide citations): physics 50/100/8/58 → 58/100/0/84; reading 29/100/0/91 → 71/100/0/100; tables 42/100/0/83 → 67/100/0/94; scanned 89/100/0/57 → 67/100/0/100; 162-slide lecture 11/89/0/0 → 63/100/0/93. Thorough reaches 67–100% coverage.
  • Summaries (recall / faithfulness): physics 83/100 → 100/100, long lecture 100/95 → 100/95, others unchanged at 89–100/100.

Install: download Lectern.dmg, drag Lectern to Applications, then right-click it and choose Open the first time (the app isn't notarized).

item.title: Pocket Pals 1.2.1
item.description: Cute desktop pets that walk on your Dock and remind you to take breaks.
item.content:encoded:
Bug fixes: continuous snow, proper snow piles with the plough, fixed text layout, Update Now button, and a big reliability pass

A quality release: no new features, just everything working the way it should.

Fixed

  • Snow no longer stops and starts. Coming back from a fullscreen app rebuilt all of Pocket Pals' windows, which threw away the snow (and, while a fullscreen app was showing, it tried to rebuild them every second). Falling snow is now its own simulation that keeps going through fullscreen apps, sleep, display changes and settings changes, eases up or down over about two seconds when you change how hard it snows, and is already falling when it first appears. Low battery pauses it below 20% and resumes above 25%, and a flickering weather forecast no longer switches it on and off.
  • The snow plough really piles up the snow. With the Dock along the bottom, the plough often stood on a surface that had no snow, so it didn't scrape anything. Now the blade scrapes the snow down to a thin dusting and pushes all of it into a bank in front of the blade, with natural sloping sides. The bank grows as you push it and stays put when you stop or turn round. A full blade spills clumps over the top, and banks tip off the end of the Dock. With the blade up you leave tyre tracks. Banks are part of the snow, shaded to match, and you can click one to make a snowball, a snowman or a fort from its snow. No snow is ever created or lost along the way.
  • The snow intensity control no longer glitches. The menus and Pet Home were being redrawn many times a second while the plough moved (and once a second otherwise), which made the Light / Medium / Blizzard control slide about. They now only update when something you can see changes.
  • Text fits. Reminder buttons no longer cut off long pet names, the Winter tab's boxes use the full width, and speech bubbles and name tags wrap neatly instead of growing very wide.
  • Walking off the end of the Dock no longer makes pals dip and "land" again (with a puff of snow) for no reason.
  • Snow landing on a tall snowbank no longer makes it smaller.
  • Old windows' memory is now freed when Pocket Pals rebuilds its windows (after display changes, waking and similar).
  • If your pets file is ever damaged, Pocket Pals now brings back your last good save instead of starting over (the damaged file is kept too).
  • Quitting with kill (or anything else that sends SIGTERM) now saves first.
  • Pocket Pals pauses while another user is using the Mac (fast user switching).

Added

  • Update Now in Settings › Updates: see what's new, then one click downloads the update, checks its signature, installs it and reopens Pocket Pals with your pals as they were. There's also Remind Me Later and Skip This Version, a progress bar with Cancel, and clear messages (with Download Manually) if anything goes wrong. Check for Updates… in the menus opens this.
  • Bring all pets back in the menu bar popover and the Help menu, and pals or items that end up off every screen come back by themselves.
  • If Pocket Pals ever closes unexpectedly, it says so kindly the next time it opens ("Your pets are safe") and offers to open a pre-filled problem report. Nothing is sent automatically.

Install: download PocketPals.dmg, drag PocketPals to Applications, then right-click it and choose Open the first time (the app isn't notarized).

item.title: Pocket Pals 1.2.0
item.description: Cute desktop pets that walk on your Dock and remind you to take breaks.
item.content:encoded:
Pets stay on your desktop, perch on minimised windows, Winter Wonderland with snow plough, and menus above the Dock

Added

  • Winter Wonderland. Turn on snow from ❄️ in the menu bar (with Light, Medium and Blizzard), or let Auto snow in your winter: June to August in the Southern Hemisphere, December to February in the Northern, worked out from your region (you can override it). With weather on, it also snows when it's really snowing outside, with real wind.
    • Snow falls in two layers of six-pointed flakes, behind your windows (or over everything, if you prefer), and scatters when you whoosh the pointer through it.
    • It settles on the Dock, on Dock icons and minimised windows, on your items, and if you like on window title bars and along the menu bar. Pals leave footprints and land with a puff; snow slides off windows you drag and tumbles off restored windows. Option-drag to wipe snow away. When snow is turned off it melts over about 30 seconds; Clear all snow is instant.
    • A snow plough you can drive. Click it, then drive with ← → or A D, Space lifts the blade and Shift goes faster. It pushes snow into piles (no snow is ever lost), with spray, an engine putter and a reversing beep. Click a pile to make a snowball, a snowman (bigger piles make bigger snowmen) or a snow fort, or flatten it. Pals ride along and chase it, and an optional auto-plough clears the Dock by itself.
    • Winter items: snowmen you can dress (hats, scarves, faces, buttons and arms) that slowly melt when the snow stops, throwable snowballs, a frozen pond pals slide on, a sled, a cosy fireplace and hot chocolate pals curl up beside, candy canes, icicles, big snowflakes and a wreath that hang from the menu bar. Right-click any item to resize (or scroll over it), duplicate or remove it, and Tidy up / Restore my winter scene in Pet Home's new Winter tab.
    • Christmas (Off, On, or Auto from 1 December to 6 January, separate from snow): a Christmas tree in three sizes with ornaments, a star or angel topper and twinkling lights, strings of fairy lights that hang like the real thing with five colour themes and five modes, presents your pals open, and an advent calendar with a little surprise behind every door.
    • Pals in winter: automatic scarves, beanies, earmuffs and boots, little puffs of breath, snow angels, catching snowflakes, digging, shaking off snow, sliding on ice, building tiny snowmen of their own, and curling up by the fire. Reindeer antlers, a Santa hat, earmuffs and boots are in the wardrobe.
    • Winter visitors: a robin flies by now and then, and a sleigh crosses the sky on Christmas Eve.
    • Snowball Fight, a seventh mini-game: aim and throw at snowman targets while your pals lob snowballs back at the pointer.
    • New sounds: wind, snow crunch, the plough's engine, scrape and beep, snowball throws, jingle bells and a music-box tune.
  • Perch on the Dock. Pals sit on Dock icons and minimised windows, choose perches by themselves (minimised windows are favourites), and react when a window is restored or the Dock hides. Drag a pal over a Dock item and it glows: let go to perch it there. Clicking the icon under a perched pal still goes straight to the Dock. Works with the Dock on the bottom, left or right. This reads where Dock items are with Accessibility permission (explained in onboarding and Settings, with an Open System Settings button); everything else works without it.
  • Where pets appear (Settings › Basic): All desktops (the default) or Only this desktop, with a Move pets to this desktop button.
  • Help › Getting Started now includes the Dock perches and a short winter tour.

Changed

  • Pets now live above the Dock, so pals perched on it, their speech bubbles and name tags are never hidden behind it. They stay below menus, notifications and the screen saver.
  • The round menu, item menus, reminder bubbles, guided breaks and the game panel now open above the Dock. Near the Dock the round menu opens as an upward half circle, right under the menu bar it opens downwards, and near the sides it shifts inwards so every button is on screen. It pops open, and you can use the arrow keys and Return, or Escape (or a click anywhere else) to close it.
  • Speech bubbles and name tags stay inside the screen: under the menu bar they move below the pal, and at the edges they shift inwards with the tail still pointing at your pal.

Fixed

  • Pals no longer appear inside fullscreen apps. The menu, reminder and game panels were allowed into fullscreen Spaces, and with "Over fullscreen apps" switched off the pets' own windows were too. Nothing joins a fullscreen Space now, and each display's pets hide instantly (and pause) while it shows a fullscreen app, then peek back when you return to a desktop. Works with multiple displays, "Displays have separate Spaces" and Stage Manager.
  • The round menu could open behind the Dock when you right-clicked a pal standing on it.
  • Weather outfits: the raincoat and scarf were never actually worn. Pals now wear them (in empty outfit slots), and splash through puddles when it rains.

Install: download PocketPals.dmg, drag PocketPals to Applications, then right-click it and choose Open the first time (the app isn't notarized).

item.title: Pocket Pals 1.1.0
item.description: Cute desktop pets that walk on your Dock and remind you to take breaks.
item.content:encoded:
30+ new animals, a simpler Pet Home, toys and beds, mini-games, pets that grow up, and much more

Added

  • 37 new animals, each with its own colours, idle animations, behaviours and sound, all drawn in code in the same soft style:
    • Aussie Mates: quokka (big smile when petted), wombat (naps bottom-first in a burrow it digs in the Dock), koala (hugs window edges and dozes), kangaroo (bounds along the Dock; a joey peeks out of an adult's pouch), platypus, echidna, sugar glider (glides between windows, hangs upside down from the menu bar), kookaburra (laughs at dawn and dusk), cockatoo (crest dance to music) and blue-tongue lizard.
    • Cute & Cosy: otter (floats on its back and holds hands with another otter), sloth, capybara (other pals sit on its head), raccoon, squirrel, guinea pig, chinchilla, ferret, mouse, lamb, piglet, pony, fawn, seal pup, polar bear cub and panda.
    • Tiny Friends: snail (a shimmering trail), bee (visits flowers and does a waggle dance), butterfly, ladybug, octopus (changes colour with its mood), jellyfish (glows in Dark Mode) and gecko.
    • Special, unlockable animals: Unicorn (friendship level 10), Phoenix (a 14-day break streak), Little Robot (adopt 10 different animals) and Ghost Cat (visits every October; keep it with the Halloween achievement). Locked animals show as silhouettes with how to unlock them.
    • New looks for old friends: beagle, poodle and dalmatian-style dogs; tortoiseshell, cream and tuxedo cats; lionhead and angora bunnies; lovebird and canary; two more red pandas (and a new "stand up tall" surprise); Emerald, Sapphire, Ruby and Gold baby dragons (who learn to breathe sparkles).
  • Pet Home, one friendly window with big tabs: My Pals, Adopt, Wardrobe, Toys & Home, Games, Reminders and Settings. Open it from the menu bar, by opening the app again, or by holding ⌃⌥P for a second.
  • Right-click a pal (or Control-click) for a round menu: Feed, Play, Pet, Trick, Sleep, Wardrobe, Hide and Pet Home.
  • Toys, beds and a desktop home: beds, food and water bowls, toys (ball, yarn, scratching post, carrot, wheel, perch, flowers, puddle, pool) and decorations (plant, a lamp that glows at night, rug, seasonal pieces). Pals use them by themselves. Drag them onto your desktop, move them around, or tidy them all away at once. Unlock them with treats, earned by taking breaks, playing and petting (treats can never be bought).
  • Six mini-games on your desktop: Fetch, Hide & Seek, Treat Catch, Copy Me, Bubble Pop and Pet Race. Each takes a minute or two, keeps a best score and earns treats and friendship.
  • Pals grow up: new pals start as babies (smaller, clumsier, sleepier), become young after 3 days and grown-ups after 10, with a little party and a diary photo each time. You can keep any pal a baby forever.
  • Tricks you can practise: tricks unlock with friendship and get smoother with practice (new ones sometimes go a bit wobbly).
  • A daily diary of cute moments ("Biscuit caught 12 balls today!"), with little snapshots you can share as a picture.
  • Pet friendships: pals who spend time together become friends, best friends nap and play together more, and you'll see hearts between them in My Pals.
  • The Pet Hotel: saying goodbye now sends a pal to the hotel with everything they've learned. Welcome them back any time.
  • Guided breaks: your pal leads a short stretch routine, a 20-20-20 eye break with a countdown, or a breathing exercise where it puffs up and down with you.
  • Study with me: your pal puts on reading glasses and studies quietly for a focus session, then celebrates and plays during the break.
  • Reminder styles: Gentle (your pal sits beside your window), Normal or Persistent. Reminders are now written as plain sentences ("Remind me to stretch every 45 minutes"), and there's a weekly break report.
  • A friendlier first run: a waving welcome, an optional "Find your perfect pal" quiz, naming with name ideas, a short interactive tutorial that ticks itself off, and one simple question about break reminders. Replay it any time from Help.
  • Shortcuts and Spotlight: Feed my pets, Call a pal, Start a break, Hide all pets, Study with me, and Shy mode.
  • Never in the way: pals move aside if the pointer rests on them while you're clicking or typing, never sit on a window's buttons or toolbar, and (optionally) keep clear of the text cursor. Shy mode sends them to the corner, small and quiet. Double-tap Option to hide them all (optional).
  • Hide automatically during screen sharing, presentations, video calls and fullscreen apps (each its own switch, all on), then peek back afterwards.
  • Name tags with a mood face above each pal: always, on hover or never.
  • Optional extras, all off until you turn them on: weather outfits (raincoats, beanies and scarves, sunglasses, snow on the Dock; weather data by Open-Meteo.com), calendar awareness (good-luck wishes before exams and interviews, quieter pals on busy days), and celebrating finished downloads. Pals also fan your Mac when it runs hot and yawn late at night.
  • Special days for your region, such as Australia Day hats, as well as adoption anniversaries, your birthday, Christmas, Easter and Halloween.
  • Pocket Pals listens for Lectern's study timer and Pulse's CPU readings, if those apps announce them, to start Study with me or fan a hot Mac.
  • VoiceOver describes each pal ("Biscuit the Corgi-style Dog, happy, sitting on the Dock"), and Pocket Pals follows Reduce Motion (no screen-crossing zoomies) and Increase Contrast (stronger outlines).

Changed

  • Adoption Centre and My Pals are now part of Pet Home, and the menu bar menu is a simple popover: your pals with Feed, Play and Call buttons, then Pet Home, Shy mode, Pause reminders and Hide all pets.
  • The menu bar icon shows your main pal's face, which changes with its mood, and a small dot when a pal needs something.
  • Settings are now split into Basic and Advanced, with a search box, an ⓘ on every option and "Restore defaults" for each section. "Pets can climb onto windows" became "Where pets can go" (Dock only, Dock and windows, or Everywhere).
  • Feeding is one click (your pal's favourite snack), with other foods a click away, instead of three menus deep.
  • "Put to sleep until I wake them" is a real setting now, rather than a year-long nap.
  • ⌃⌥P: tap to hide or show pals as before; hold it for a second to open Pet Home.
  • Uses less energy: lower frame rates when pals are idle or asleep, far fewer window checks, and textures that are drawn once and kept on disk.

Fixed

  • If an overlay window ever goes missing, Pocket Pals makes a new one, and pals that end up off screen (for example after unplugging a display) walk back into view.

Install: download PocketPals.dmg, drag PocketPals to Applications, then right-click it and choose Open the first time (the app isn't notarized).

item.title: Lectern 1.6.0
item.description: Subjects, lecture notes, flashcards, quizzes and a planner in one Mac app.
item.content:encoded:
Summary Studio with fact-checked summaries, study modes, past papers, Listen, semantic search, quick capture and references

This is the "1.2.0" feature release. It's numbered 1.6.0 because Lectern 1.5.3 is already installed and updates can only go forward.

Added

  • Summary Studio (wand button on every page, ⇧⌘S): 17 formats (bullets, numbered, checklist, outline, paragraphs, Cornell, three table styles, Q&A, glossary, mind map, timeline, flowchart, one-page cheat sheet, TL;DR, slide by slide, formula sheet, layered, custom); lengths from TL;DR to comprehensive or a word count, with a word and reading-time estimate; level, focus areas and keywords; include/exclude citations, examples, formulas, diagrams, "things to clarify" and exam questions; output language with bilingual key terms; six built-in presets plus your own, with defaults per subject and page type; insert into the page's Summary section, at the cursor, as a new page or to the clipboard.
  • A new fact-based summary engine: facts first (cached by file and settings, so changing format or length is quick), then writing, then every statement checked against its slides. Unconfirmed statements are marked "⚠ check" with the source on hover. Coverage is checked per slide (per topic for short summaries) and a report line shows slides covered, topics, statements verified, the model and the time. Prompts live in editable files with worked examples; temperatures are 0.2 for facts and checks and 0.5 for writing; small models get smaller sections and topic-by-topic writing.
  • Layered summaries (TL;DR, then key points that expand, then slide references), "Summarise together" for several pages with citations like [Slides 12] [Reading p. 4] [Recording 14:32], and week, topic and subject summaries built from page summaries.
  • Mind maps, timelines and flowcharts drawn by Lectern, with zoom, PNG/SVG export and "Edit as Outline".
  • Per-section tools (Regenerate, Shorter, Longer, Simpler, More examples, Change format, Verify again), format changes without AI for lists and tables, 👍/👎 ratings that adjust your defaults, and summary version history with side-by-side compare and restore.
  • Summarise All… and a Processing Queue window: progress and time left, pause, resume, cancel, drag to reorder, carries on after a restart, can wait until the Mac is plugged in and idle, and notifies you when done.
  • Better reading of files: titles, headings, nesting and reading order (including two-column PDFs), tables from PDF, PowerPoint and Word, speaker notes, formulas as maths, on-device OCR with automatic language detection and a confidence note, and topic detection. Clean-up removes repeated headers and footers, slide numbers, copyright lines, "Questions?"/"Thank you"/agenda/blank slides and build-up duplicates, and joins "(cont.)" slides, with a "Cleaned: removed N…" note you can open.
  • New sources: .srt and .vtt captions, transcripts with timestamps, recordings matched to slides, EPUB books by chapter, images and handwriting by OCR, and web articles with their title, author and date.

  • Each request has a priority, so what you're looking at always comes first and background extras pause first when the allowance runs low.
  • The ⌘1 … ⌘9 sections are listed in the View menu, and each section keeps its place when you switch away and back. The last section is remembered between launches.

  • Invalid keys, per-minute limits, daily limits and network errors each get their own correct message.

Text, speaker notes and diagram images are extracted; long decks are written in parts then merged. Notes include an overview, objectives, topic notes with clickable slide citations, diagrams explained, key terms (added to the subject glossary), a summary, likely exam questions and things to clarify. A cost estimate is shown first, and every step can be cancelled.

  • Study Coach per subject (advice from assessments, flashcards, quizzes, confidence ratings and study time; evidence-based techniques; “Plan my week”) and “Ask about this subject”, answered from your own notes with clickable sources.
  • Home dashboard, week/month planner with drag-to-reschedule, optional Apple Calendar sync, a Pomodoro study timer in the menu bar, and a grade calculator with Australian grade bands.
  • Global search (pages, slide text, transcripts and flashcards), command palette (⌘K), recent and pinned pages, back/forward, subject glossary.
  • Export a page, folder or subject as PDF (with a cover page), Markdown or HTML; print; a subject study guide PDF; copy as Markdown; one-click full backup zip.
  • Version history (the last 50 versions of each page) with preview and restore.

Fixes for Bluetooth audio, the permission prompt, overlays and recording

Fixed

item.title: Resonance 1.0.0
item.description: A music visualiser for your Mac that reacts to whatever is playing.
item.content:encoded:
First release

Added

  • Listens to whatever your Mac is playing: system audio (Core Audio process tap, all apps or only the apps you choose, such as Spotify), with screen-capture audio and any input device (microphone, BlackHole) as fallbacks.
  • Real-time music analysis: 64 frequency bands, bass, mids and treble, loudness, automatic gain so quiet and loud songs both look great, beat detection with tempo (60–180 BPM), bar position and beat anticipation, and build-up and drop detection for big moments.
  • 18 original scenes: Neon Tunnel, Particle Galaxy (up to 2 million stars), Liquid Chrome, Aurora Waves, Kaleidoscope Bloom, 3D Spectrum City, Circular Spectrum (with album art), Ink Fluid, Synthwave Grid, Oscilloscope, Firework Beats, Lava Lamp, Warp Speed, Sound Terrain, Plasma Pulse, Ribbon Dance, Crystal Cave and Minimal Wave. Each has its own parameters.
  • Shuffle (a new scene for every track) and Auto-VJ (switches scenes on drops or every 16, 32 or 64 bars, with beat-synced crossfade, zoom blur, glitch, ripple and white-flash transitions, never repeating a scene, optionally favourites only).
  • Glow and polish on every scene: HDR bloom, chromatic aberration, film grain, vignette, trails and an optional kaleidoscope. Low, Medium, High and Ultra quality plus render scale.
  • 16 built-in palettes, an Album Art palette made from the current song's cover, a gradient editor for your own palettes, and palette behaviours (static, hue drift, cycle every N bars, accent flash on drops).
  • Display modes: window, fullscreen on any display (cursor hides, Mac stays awake), a live wallpaper behind your windows, a click-through overlay on top (opacity, normal or additive blending, full screen, bottom band or corner), a floating mini player, a live spectrum in the menu bar icon, and a Resonance screen saver.
  • Song title cards and play/pause/skip controls for Music and Spotify.
  • Screenshots (⌘S) and 10, 30 or 60-second MP4 clips with the audio (⌘R), at up to 1080p60.
  • Photosensitivity warning on first launch and Reduce Flashing on by default (fewer than 3 large brightness changes per second, softened strobes, capped glow). Reduce Motion is respected.
  • Single-key shortcuts (arrows, Space, C, F, O, M, H, R, 1–9, Esc, ?), presets, favourites, onboarding with a live level meter, Settings, and automatic updates.

Install: download Resonance.dmg, drag Resonance to Applications, then right-click it and choose Open the first time (the app isn't notarized).

item.title: Midnight Roulette 1.0.0

item.content:encoded:
Added

  • European single-zero roulette with every standard bet: straight up, splits (including 0-1, 0-2, 0-3), streets, trios, corners, First Four, six lines, columns, dozens and the six even-money bets.
  • A smooth 3D wheel built entirely from procedural meshes and shaders, with a ball path that is planned to land in the result drawn when you press Spin. Normal (~10 s), fast (~4 s) and instant modes, plus an optional ball-following camera.
  • A vertical betting table with exact click zones for every bet, hover previews, drag-to-move stacks, undo, rebet, double and saved bet layouts ("My Bets").
  • Racetrack call bets: Voisins du Zéro, Tiers du Cylindre, Orphelins, Jeu Zéro and neighbours bets.
  • Dolly, rake and payout animations, and tasteful celebrations for straight-up, big and huge wins.
  • Results history (last 500 spins), statistics for the last 100 spins and all time, hot/cold numbers and an optional heat overlay.
  • Configurable table limits, La Partage, extra $500/$1,000 chips, casino-mode betting timer and swap-panels layout.
  • Original synthesised sound effects, lounge music and casino ambience; optional dealer voice using the computer's text-to-speech.
  • Accessibility: colour-blind markers, text size 80–150%, reduce motion, full keyboard and controller support.
  • Wellbeing reminders and a clear play-money-only notice.
  • Auto-save after every bet and spin (atomic writes) with safe recovery if the game closes mid-spin.
  • In-game update checker that looks for new releases on GitHub.

item.title: Driftscape 1.0.0
item.description: Live wallpapers that follow your real sky, weather and music.
item.content:encoded:
First release

Added

  • Live wallpapers on every display and every Space, drawn behind your desktop icons with Metal, including behind the menu bar and notch.
  • 38 original, procedurally generated wallpapers in six collections: Water, Rain & Windows, Space, Nature, City & Cosy and Abstract.
  • Real time of day: the sun's position for your location drives sunrise colours, golden hour, dusk and starry nights, with the moon in its real phase.
  • Real weather from Open-Meteo every 30 minutes: clouds, rain, snow, fog, wind and thunderstorms fade in smoothly (rain takes two minutes to arrive). A weather preview menu lets you try Clear, Cloudy, Rain, Storm, Snow and Fog.
  • Optional music reactivity (off by default): wallpapers breathe gently with what your Mac is playing, using system audio, screen-capture audio or an input device. Sound is analysed live and never recorded.
  • Library with live hover previews, collections, search and favourites.
  • Studio with a large live preview, automatic controls for every setting, time/weather/music toggles, Randomize, Reset, undo and redo, and Save as Preset.
  • Schedules by time of day (dawn, sunrise, day, golden hour, sunset, night or set times) or a shuffle playlist, with crossfades.
  • A different wallpaper for each display.
  • Export a 5K still (PNG) or a seamless 10-second loop (MP4).
  • Lock screen and Mission Control kept in step with a still frame every 15 minutes, with your own wallpaper restored when you quit.
  • A Driftscape screen saver, installed with one click from Settings.
  • Energy saving: 30 fps at 75% resolution by default, and a complete pause when the desktop is covered, the screen is locked or asleep, in Low Power Mode or (optionally) on battery. A live CPU and GPU readout in Settings.
  • Menu bar menu, onboarding, Settings, automatic updates and a screen saver.

item.title: Wanderfund 1.0.0
item.description: Plan trips, find good-value dates and track spending while you're away.
item.content:encoded:
First release

Added

  • Trip planner with a friendly five-step wizard: city search with autocomplete, multi-city stops, fixed or flexible dates, travellers, travel style and accommodation.
  • Budget engine with a bundled dataset of 181 destinations (estimates at three travel styles), seasonal pricing, distance-based flight estimates, insurance, eSIM, shopping and an emergency buffer, all converted to your home currency.
  • Smart suggestions (hostel nights, shoulder season, food budget) and a Tight / Realistic / Comfortable reality check on every budget.
  • Date Finder: a 12-month value calendar and the top 5 date windows from your home airport, using seasons, NSW school holidays, public holidays, weather history, day of week and booking timing. Optional live flight prices with your own SerpApi or Duffel key, plus daily price watches.
  • Exchange: live ECB rates via Frankfurter, a converter, 90-day charts compared with the average, rate alerts and a travel money planner.
  • Study Exchange mode with a monthly budget, income and funding (including OS-HELP), shortfall or surplus, and a semester timeline.
  • Savings goals with progress rings, weekly/fortnightly/monthly targets, projections, a "what if" slider, reminders and milestone confetti.
  • Expenses in any currency with the day's rate stored, receipt scanning, cost splitting and settle up, a daily budget tracker and bank CSV import.
  • Reports with interactive charts, PDF trip reports and CSV export.
  • Day-by-day itinerary with maps, and packing, documents and before-you-go checklists (with passport expiry warnings).
  • Optional "Ask Wanderfund" assistant using your own Claude API key.
  • Dashboard with countdown, savings, payments due, rates, alerts and a world map; a menu bar helper; onboarding; JSON backups; and automatic updates.
